A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Hydra-SGG and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The implementation, pseudocode, and failure cases can be matched across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original Hydra-SGG benchmark results, component ablations, sensitivity experiments, and qualitative predictions.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark and diagnostic results and adds query-distance analysis and loss-weight experiments.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 and the appendix pseudocode retain the assignment rule, shared decoder branches, losses, and inference procedure. The additional loss-weight experiments test alternatives without changing the adopted equal-weight objective.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate SGDet on VG150, Open Images V6, and GQA, and retain the same Unsplash examples and appendix failure cases. The added diagnostics use existing VG150 coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds SSR-CNN as an evaluated comparator; v1 only cited its underlying work. New Table 4g adds a focused VG150 comparison with TDE, NICE, IETrans, CFA, VETO, and NICEST. Existing benchmark comparator sets are otherwise retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds F-Recall reporting in Table 1, a query-distance protocol covering 300 queries on 5,000 validation images, and a loss-weight sweep from 1:0.5 to 1:3. Benchmark splits and stated default epoch budgets remain unchanged. Removed training disclosures do not establish changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: Section 3.4 adds a targeted analysis of whether removing self-attention brings query embeddings closer together. Table 4f adds sensitivity to the relative assignment-loss weights. Existing component, threshold, epoch, query-count, diversity-score, and failure-case analyses remain.

E5.justification: V2 introduces uncertainty entries for Hydra-SGG across all three benchmark tables and a paired t-test with Cohen's d for query distances; these reporting practices are absent from v1. However, the new ± notation is undefined, and no run or seed counts are supplied, so additional repeated runs cannot be established.

E6.justification: V2 adds F-Recall results, comparator entries, loss-weight outcomes, and query-distance findings. Benchmark entries also change: VG150 mR@50 becomes 15.9±0.2 instead of 16.0, Open Images weighted score becomes 50.0±0.2 instead of 50.1, and GQA mR@50 becomes 12.5±0.2 instead of 12.7. Since the aggregation is unexplained and earlier values remain in prose, these changes do not establish performance deterioration. Section 4.3 also corrects vanilla mR@50 from 16.0 to 14.9, matching the unchanged Table 4a.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, the assignment-score definition, and Diversity Score remain unchanged. No theorem, proof, or formal derivation is added. F-Recall is an additional standard evaluation metric, and Section 3.4 reports empirical statistics.

C1.justification: The hybrid-assignment, Hydra Branch, fast-convergence, and state-of-the-art claims remain. V2's abstract drops the explicit 'for the first time' priority claim for the self-attention finding, modestly narrowing the novelty assertion.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of loss-weight tradeoffs and rare-relation gains, plus limitations concerning manually designed assignments and training noise in Appendix D. Its six-queries-per-category explanation in Section 4.2 conflicts with the retained per-ground-truth selection in Section 3.2. The speculative warning about DSGG's undisclosed backbone is removed.

D1.justification: V2 deletes the Section 4.1 implementation paragraph without relocating its AdamW optimizer, initial learning rate of 2e-4, batch size of 16, six-layer encoder/decoder, and eight-attention-head specifications. This substantially reduces reproducibility information despite retaining appendix schedules and preprocessing. V2 adds a repository link for a promised code/model release, but the PDFs do not establish availability.

R1.justification: Related work adds citations concerning LLM-assisted scene graphs, recent interaction detection, and debiasing, including NICEST and IETrans. References such as Swin Transformer and Anchor DETR are removed. The one-stage discussion sharpens the contrast between prior query/architecture designs and Hydra-SGG's training-efficiency focus without changing the overall positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and parts of related work are rewritten; qualitative discussion and the conclusion are shortened. V2 adds Section 3.4, renumbers appendices, and updates publication and author annotations, while retaining the overall narrative and most method prose.

P2.justification: Tables 1 and 3 consolidate recall columns, Table 1 adds F-Recall columns, and Tables 1–3 accommodate uncertainty entries. Table 4 gains panels f and g. Existing figures are retained, while the appendix failure figure is relabeled S1 and the pseudocode display is reformatted.

improvement.justification: The new query-distance analysis, loss-weight sweep, and comparator results strengthen empirical support. However, v2 removes important reproducibility settings, leaves its uncertainty notation unexplained, and introduces a category-balancing explanation inconsistent with Section 3.2. These substantive validation gains and reproducibility/consistency losses prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
